decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts build directly on the core polishing and drilling competence, so carrying them costs little while demand for wafer-level packaging keeps growing.
Carrier wafers for handling smaller diameters are a low-cost extension of the standard carrier line and fit the strategic push toward reusable carriers.

The Cu-interposer is a still-uncertain option on advanced packaging demand that was launched prominently at SEMICON, so keeping it while the uncertainty resolves is worth more than its modest carrying cost.
The off-the-shelf Wafer Universe brand sells standard products close to the core business at little extra cost and widens market reach.

Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the core and costlier to sustain, but their value is not yet clearly disproven and the firm holds few other options, so it likely keeps them for now despite a substantial risk of dropping.
